Description: God’s heart has always been for the nations. This October, ACAC will celebrate Missions Month 2026: Known Among the Nations, a month devoted to recognizing what God is doing around the world and considering our own part in His mission. Together, we’ll hear stories of God at work, celebrate the people and ministries carrying the gospel across cultures and borders, and be challenged to consider how God might use each of us to make Jesus known. text:

Recurs: Every Wed – Sun, weekly
Venue: Wood Street Galleries, 601 Wood St, Pittsburgh, PA 15222, USA
Organizer: Pittsburgh Cultural Trust
Description: Sound of the City is an immersive audio installation and listening environment by NYC born artist and composer Hprizm, whose practice spans a wide array of genres, including music, performance and multimedia installations. He is a co-founder of the seminal hip-hop group Antipop Consortium, an experimental collective known for their lyrical approach to electronic music.
Centered on a sonic score that moves between abstract noise and melodic interludes, Sound of the City collapses vinyl records, tape loops and granular synthesis with audio footage captured by Hprizm over the past few years. Wielding his phone as a primary recording device, the artist took notice of his sonic environment while traversing New York City and western Pennsylvania, where he partially resides. In his own words, “The sound of the city, in a literal sense, is dense. Buried histories rumble beneath the foundation of brick. Crate digging and knowledge of self unearthed a cultural medium that informs my process.”
For Hprizm, sound carries strong implications—not only about personal narrative, but about socioeconomic conditions and resources as well. He writes, “Within the throughline for most of my work is an interrelation between memory and sonic imprints. Organizer: DEMASKUS Theater Collective
Description: A reimagining of the classic work by Shakespeare, Othello of the End Zone follows the journey and battles of Imani Othello who must navigate the treacherous world of sports and her own insecurities after being named Head Coach of America's most beloved football franchise. The language is updated, the setting transformed, but the emotional truth is intact: a Black woman at the height of her power, navigating a world designed to doubt her — not as a tragic pawn, but as a fully realized human being. The adaptation explores the price of ambition and asks: "When a woman shatters a glass ceiling, what waits for her when she lands?"

Description: What the F**k Was That? This hilarious show takes all the elements of the cult classic films The Evil Dead, Evil Dead 2, and Army of Darkness and combines them into one of the craziest theatrical experiences of all time. Five college students go to an abandoned cabin in the woods and accidentally unleash an evil force that turns them all into demons. It's all up to Ash (a housewares employee turned demon-killing hero) and his trusty chainsaw to save the day. Blood flies. Limbs are dismembered. Demons tell bad jokes ... and all to music. The songs in the show are completely off the wall. Titles like "All the Men in My Life Keep Getting Killed by Candarian Demons" and "What the F**k Was That?" will have audiences rolling in their seats and screaming for more and more blood.

Description: With a special introduction by producer Ted Haynes, Q&A after the film, and live music on stage! OCCUPATIONAL HAZARD: THE FIRST CORAL REEFERS is a feature documentary that journeys back to the 1970s and early 1980s to tell the story of Jimmy Buffett’s original Coral Reefer Band. Set against the creative backdrop of Key West, the film explores the musicians, friendships, touring years, and studio sessions that helped shape Buffett’s legendary sound. Through rare, never-before-seen archival footage and deeply personal interviews with founding members, tour managers, producers and music legends, OCCUPATIONAL HAZARD captures the camaraderie, chaos, and magic of an era that thrived on freedom and lived without a rulebook. Narrated by Academy-award winner Jeff Bridges, OCCUPATIONAL HAZARD offers fans a deeper look at the people behind the music and the era that helped define Jimmy Buffett’s lasting legacy. This film is a tribute to Buffett and the original Coral Reefers, the places and people that shaped them, the volatile beauty of a musical moment that couldn’t last but changed everything and their candid sentiment toward Buffett. It’s the origin story upon which the Parrot Head empire was built upon, by the people who helped lay the foundation. Directed by John H. Description: Fiasco Theater and The Public partner to celebrate a hidden American classic: THE VERGE by Susan Glaspell, Pulitzer Prize winner and founder of the Provincetown Players. In Glaspell’s 1921 masterpiece, botanist Claire Archer is on a quest to create a new life: a plant unlike any that has ever come before. When her husband, lover, and soulmate each arrive in her greenhouse seeking heat in a snowstorm, chaos ensues. But as Claire pushes–sometimes violently—against the constraints of her own good breeding, she wonders if the only way to transcend boundaries is to destroy them. By turns witty farce, devastating philosophical debate, and scathing feminist cry, THE VERGE defies genre and pierces the bounds of theatrical realism. Jessie Austrian directs this new Fiasco production, featuring Tony Award winner Miriam Silverman.

Description: Sound of the City is an immersive audio installation and listening environment by NYC born artist and composer Hprizm, whose practice spans a wide array of genres, including music, performance and multimedia installations. He is a co-founder of the seminal hip-hop group Antipop Consortium, an experimental collective known for their lyrical approach to electronic music.
Centered on a sonic score that moves between abstract noise and melodic interludes, Sound of the City collapses vinyl records, tape loops and granular synthesis with audio footage captured by Hprizm over the past few years. Wielding his phone as a primary recording device, the artist took notice of his sonic environment while traversing New York City and western Pennsylvania, where he partially resides. Description: New 4K restoration! Fifty-five years after its initial release, the definitive version of The Devils is now returning to theaters this October! Fully restored in 4K and cut to Ken Russell’s specific direction, Ken Russell’s The Devils is the first publicly released version of the film as intended by the filmmaker. Ken Russell’s controversial adaptation of Aldous Huxley’s The Devils of Loudun is at long last available in its full, provocative splendor. This new restoration thrillingly incorporates material that was originally censored—footage that Russell deemed some of the best and most political work of his career. A young Derek Jarman designed the sets that house this story of a vengeful nun (Vanessa Redgrave) who accuses a priest (Oliver Reed) of collaborating with the devil, resulting in the apparent possession of an entire convent. A fearless account of state and church corruption, The Devils mixes graphic sexual imagery with religious iconography in an unforgettable spectacle that could only issue from the mind of Ken Russell. In addition to powerhouse performances from Reed and Redgrave, Ken Russell’s The Devils showcases the stunning work of artists at the peak of their craft: Academy Award-winning cinematographer David Watkin ( Out of Africa , Chariots of Fire ); editor Michael Bradsell ( Local Hero , Jabberwocky ); and visual artist Derek Jarman, whose work as production designer marks his feature film debut. title: Public Utility Commission (Friday, October 30, 2026)
text:
Public Utility Commission runs from Friday, October 30, 2026 to Sunday, March 7, 2027 at The Goddard School of Pittsburgh - Downtown.
Event: Public Utility Commission
Date: Friday, October 30, 2026 at 11:00 AM to Sunday, March 7, 2027 at 5:00 PM
Recurs: Runs Oct 30 – Mar 7 (129 days)
Venue: The Goddard School of Pittsburgh - Downtown, 812 Liberty Ave, Pittsburgh, PA 15222
Organizer: Pittsburgh Cultural Trust
Price: Free
Description: A public utility commission is the regulatory body that oversees providers of essential services, such as water, gas, electricity, rail, and transportation, among others. In practice, corporate capture has often led to these bodies running cover for private corporations with monopolistic reach. How they behave in the dawning era of data center buildouts is a shadow looming on the horizon. If we reconsidered ‘public utility’ in the broadest manner, what might that phrase suggest? What would it look like if there were such a commission dedicated to all the little problems and solutions of making life more functional, and fruitful? And what if governance were so shaped that it was our working partner in that realization of our shared reality, down to those minute details? The exhibition “Public Utility Commission” is an attempt to dial that imagination into some clarity. As such, it is a reflection on privatization and fundamental issues of human spirit—like what we owe one another, and the shared responsibilities to those we exist beside—while predatory forces do their best to pollute and diminish the spaces we tenuously hold together. “Public Utility Commission” features the work of a robust roster of artists—internationally, from England, France, Italy, and the Republic of Georgia; regionally, from Lancaster, Morgantown, Philadelphia, and New York City; and many, locally, from Pittsburgh. “Public Utility Commission” is designed and curated by Jacquet Kehm and presented by the

Description: With a legendary career spanning more than five decades, KANSAS has firmly established itself as one of the most iconic bands in classic rock history. Since emerging from Topeka, Kansas, and releasing its self-titled debut album in 1974, the band has sold more than 30 million albums worldwide.

KANSAS has released 16 studio albums and five live albums, earning eight gold albums, three sextuple-platinum albums, a platinum live album, and multi-platinum singles including the classic rock staples "Carry On Wayward Son" and "Dust in the Wind." The band's music dominated the charts throughout the 1970s and 1980s, with KANSAS appearing on the Billboard charts for more than 200 weeks and performing to sold-out arenas across North America, Europe, and Japan.

Description: Sound of the City is an immersive audio installation and listening environment by NYC born artist and composer Hprizm, whose practice spans a wide array of genres, including music, performance and multimedia installations. He is a co-founder of the seminal hip-hop group Antipop Consortium, an experimental collective known for their lyrical approach to electronic music.
Centered on a sonic score that moves between abstract noise and melodic interludes, Sound of the City collapses vinyl records, tape loops and granular synthesis with audio footage captured by Hprizm over the past few years. Wielding his phone as a primary recording device, the artist took notice of his sonic environment while traversing New York City and western Pennsylvania, where he partially resides. In his own words, “The sound of the city, in a literal sense, is dense. Buried histories rumble beneath the foundation of brick. Crate digging and knowledge of self unearthed a cultural medium that informs my process.”
For Hprizm, sound carries strong implications—not only about personal narrative, but about socioeconomic conditions and resources as well. Description: Come see how the world could be. Welcome to HADESTOWN, where a song can change your fate. Winner of eight 2019 Tony Awards® including Best Musical and the 2020 Grammy® Award for Best Musical Theater Album, this acclaimed new show by celebrated singersongwriter Anaïs Mitchell and innovative director Rachel Chavkin (Natasha, Pierre & The Great Comet of 1812) is a love story for today... and always.

HADESTOWN intertwines two mythic tales — that of young dreamers Orpheus and Eurydice, and that of King Hades and his wife Persephone — as it invites you on a hell-raising journey to the underworld and back. Mitchell’s beguiling melodies and Chavkin’s poetic imagination pit industry against nature, doubt against faith, and fear against love. Performed by a vibrant ensemble of actors, dancers and singers, HADESTOWN is a haunting and hopeful theatrical experience that grabs you and never lets go.

Description: New 4K Restoration! Begotten has no characters in the ordinary sense. Its final credits name three principal figures: God Killing Himself. Mother Earth. Son of Earth — Flesh on Bone The entire film is what those names do to each other and to the earth. God Killing Himself tears open his body and dies. Mother Earth rises from what remains and takes his seed into herself. She gives birth to Son of Earth — Flesh on Bone. He is cast into a barren world, seized by the Nomads, tortured, killed, and briefly returned to life by his mother. The Nomads destroy her too. The Robed Figures gather what remains of mother and son, grind their bodies down, and return them to the soil. The ground flowers. Begotten was shot in black and white on 16mm reversal film, then rephotographed frame by frame through neutral-density filters. The process took four years and roughly ten hours of work for every finished minute. The image was worked by hand through repeated exposure and filtration until the grain itself began to move like an atmospheric condition, thickening the dark and tearing open the light. When the film first began circulating, no one agreed on where it belonged. Drama. Horror. Foreign. In one San Francisco video store, briefly, pornography. Susan Sontag encountered the film through the festival circuit, became one of its earliest and most important advocates and began showing it to people in her living room. text:

Event: Chronovisor

Recurs: Runs Nov 3 – Nov 14 (12 days)
Venue: Pittsburgh Cultural Trust, 809 Liberty Ave Pittsburgh, PA 15222
Organizer: Pittsburgh Cultural Trust
Description: Benedictine monk Father Pellegrino Ernetti claimed to have invented, alongside Enrico Fermi and Wernher von Braun, a device called the Chronovisor, capable of transmitting events of the past as if live on TV. He professed to have witnessed orations by Cicero and the Crucifixion, though the evidence he provided, reported in the Italian press, was widely disputed. Taking this as their jumping-off point, filmmakers Kevin Walker and Jack Auen engage in a form of time travel as well, following Columbia scholar Béatrice Courte (real-life professor Anne-Laure Sellier), who comes across the Chronovisor while researching an unrelated topic and then, like countless hyperlink- or microfiche-surfing grad students before her, gets lost on an academic side quest. Traveling deeper and deeper into a stubbornly analog archive, she unearths an elaborate web of conjecture and conspiracy reaching all the way up to the highest echelons of the Vatican. Dense with on-screen text from real primary sources, scored to music by Gustav Holst, and shot on 16mm in the pooling shadows of many of New York City’s historic libraries, Chronovisor is a witty literary mystery about one of the many secrets that still hide out in libraries, waiting for someone with time, curiosity, and a JSTOR login to come along and disturb the dusty stacks - one of the year’s most singular and formally assured feature debuts. Description: Sound of the City is an immersive audio installation and listening environment by NYC born artist and composer Hprizm, whose practice spans a wide array of genres, including music, performance and multimedia installations. He is a co-founder of the seminal hip-hop group Antipop Consortium, an experimental collective known for their lyrical approach to electronic music.
Centered on a sonic score that moves between abstract noise and melodic interludes, Sound of the City collapses vinyl records, tape loops and granular synthesis with audio footage captured by Hprizm over the past few years. Wielding his phone as a primary recording device, the artist took notice of his sonic environment while traversing New York City and western Pennsylvania, where he partially resides. In his own words, “The sound of the city, in a literal sense, is dense. Buried histories rumble beneath the foundation of brick. Crate digging and knowledge of self unearthed a cultural medium that informs my process.”
For Hprizm, sound carries strong implications—not only about personal narrative, but about socioeconomic conditions and resources as well. He writes, “Within the throughline for most of my work is an interrelation between memory and sonic imprints. Category: drink
Organizer: City Winery Pittsburgh
Description: Ami Taf Ra brings her sweeping, cross cultural sound to City Winery Pittsburgh this November, joined by acclaimed saxophonist, composer, and producer K amasi Washington for a tour presentation of her debut album, The Prophet and the Madman. Produced by Washington and released on Brainfeeder, the album draws on Moroccan Gnawa, Arabic musical tradition, gospel, soul, and spiritual jazz, inspired in part by Kahlil Gibran's writing on healing and ancestral memory. Ami's commanding, operatic voice carries the record from intimacy to theatrical release.
The partnership between Ami and Washington anchors the project, heard most clearly on "How I Became a Madman," a meditation on the tension between chaos and clarity. Together they build something that feels both rooted in tradition and pointed toward what comes next, connecting North African and Middle Eastern music with the improvisational spirit of contemporary jazz.
Ami's international resume includes performances across Europe, North Africa, the Middle East, and the United States, among them the Dutch Royal Metropole Orchestra, the Hollywood Bowl Jazz Festival, and City Winery Boston. Washington, a Grammy winner and Emmy nominee, remains one of his generation's defining musical voices, moving fluently between jazz, soul, hip hop, classical, and screen work.

Description: Sound of the City is an immersive audio installation and listening environment by NYC born artist and composer Hprizm, whose practice spans a wide array of genres, including music, performance and multimedia installations. He is a co-founder of the seminal hip-hop group Antipop Consortium, an experimental collective known for their lyrical approach to electronic music.
Centered on a sonic score that moves between abstract noise and melodic interludes, Sound of the City collapses vinyl records, tape loops and granular synthesis with audio footage captured by Hprizm over the past few years. Wielding his phone as a primary recording device, the artist took notice of his sonic environment while traversing New York City and western Pennsylvania, where he partially resides. In his own words, “The sound of the city, in a literal sense, is dense. Buried histories rumble beneath the foundation of brick. Crate digging and knowledge of self unearthed a cultural medium that informs my process.”

Organizer: Pittsburgh Cultural Trust
Description: Sound of the City is an immersive audio installation and listening environment by NYC born artist and composer Hprizm, whose practice spans a wide array of genres, including music, performance and multimedia installations. He is a co-founder of the seminal hip-hop group Antipop Consortium, an experimental collective known for their lyrical approach to electronic music.
Centered on a sonic score that moves between abstract noise and melodic interludes, Sound of the City collapses vinyl records, tape loops and granular synthesis with audio footage captured by Hprizm over the past few years. Wielding his phone as a primary recording device, the artist took notice of his sonic environment while traversing New York City and western Pennsylvania, where he partially resides. In his own words, “The sound of the city, in a literal sense, is dense. Buried histories rumble beneath the foundation of brick. Crate digging and knowledge of self unearthed a cultural medium that informs my process.”
For Hprizm, sound carries strong implications—not only about personal narrative, but about socioeconomic conditions and resources as well. Description: Sound of the City is an immersive audio installation and listening environment by NYC born artist and composer Hprizm, whose practice spans a wide array of genres, including music, performance and multimedia installations. He is a co-founder of the seminal hip-hop group Antipop Consortium, an experimental collective known for their lyrical approach to electronic music.
Centered on a sonic score that moves between abstract noise and melodic interludes, Sound of the City collapses vinyl records, tape loops and granular synthesis with audio footage captured by Hprizm over the past few years. Wielding his phone as a primary recording device, the artist took notice of his sonic environment while traversing New York City and western Pennsylvania, where he partially resides. In his own words, “The sound of the city, in a literal sense, is dense. Buried histories rumble beneath the foundation of brick. Crate digging and knowledge of self unearthed a cultural medium that informs my process.”
For Hprizm, sound carries strong implications—not only about personal narrative, but about socioeconomic conditions and resources as well. Description: Pittsburgh Ballet Theatre (PBT)’s Pointe in Time fundraiser is a top 10 annual event that brings over 400 arts patrons together in support of PBT’s mainstage programming, arts education in schools and community centers, classes for individuals with disabilities, and funding for its Bridge Scholarship program. Scholarships cover all tuition costs (school year and summer) as well as associated costs (pointe shoes, leotards and tights) which can cost up to $70,000 per student.
For 57 years, Pittsburgh Ballet Theatre has inspired our community and made it a more beautiful place – on the stage, in the studio and in our neighborhoods. Join us in celebrating PBT’s Season of Wonder!
The evening includes a multi-course dining experience for guests as they enjoy exclusive world-premiere performances by PBT company artists and PBT School students. A silent and live auction, pointe shoe raffle, and dancing are all a part of the night’s festivities.
We invite you to gather family, friends, colleagues and clients, and join us for an unforgettable night celebrating PBT’s world-class art and life-changing programs.

title: Hprizm: Sound of the City (Wednesday, November 18, 2026)
text:
Hprizm: Sound of the City takes place on Wednesday, November 18, 2026 at 11:00 AM at Wood Street Galleries.
Event: Hprizm: Sound of the City
Date: Wednesday, November 18, 2026 at 11:00 AM to 4:00 PM
Recurs: Every Wed – Sun, weekly
Venue: Wood Street Galleries, 601 Wood St, Pittsburgh, PA 15222, USA
Organizer: Pittsburgh Cultural Trust
Description: Sound of the City is an immersive audio installation and listening environment by NYC born artist and composer Hprizm, whose practice spans a wide array of genres, including music, performance and multimedia installations. He is a co-founder of the seminal hip-hop group Antipop Consortium, an experimental collective known for their lyrical approach to electronic music.
Centered on a sonic score that moves between abstract noise and melodic interludes, Sound of the City collapses vinyl records, tape loops and granular synthesis with audio footage captured by Hprizm over the past few years. Wielding his phone as a primary recording device, the artist took notice of his sonic environment while traversing New York City and western Pennsylvania, where he partially resides. In his own words, “The sound of the city, in a literal sense, is dense. Buried histories rumble beneath the foundation of brick. Crate digging and knowledge of self unearthed a cultural medium that informs my process.”
For Hprizm, sound carries strong implications—not only about personal narrative, but about socioeconomic conditions and resources as well. He writes, “Within the throughline for most of my work is an interrelation between memory and sonic imprints. Description: Sound of the City is an immersive audio installation and listening environment by NYC born artist and composer Hprizm, whose practice spans a wide array of genres, including music, performance and multimedia installations. He is a co-founder of the seminal hip-hop group Antipop Consortium, an experimental collective known for their lyrical approach to electronic music.
Centered on a sonic score that moves between abstract noise and melodic interludes, Sound of the City collapses vinyl records, tape loops and granular synthesis with audio footage captured by Hprizm over the past few years. Wielding his phone as a primary recording device, the artist took notice of his sonic environment while traversing New York City and western Pennsylvania, where he partially resides. In his own words, “The sound of the city, in a literal sense, is dense. Buried histories rumble beneath the foundation of brick. Crate digging and knowledge of self unearthed a cultural medium that informs my process.”
For Hprizm, sound carries strong implications—not only about personal narrative, but about socioeconomic conditions and resources as well. title: I Will Belong To Only Me (Sunday, November 22, 2026)
text:
I Will Belong To Only Me runs from Sunday, November 22, 2026 to Friday, April 30, 2027 at August Wilson African American Cultural Center.
Event: I Will Belong To Only Me
Date: Sunday, November 22, 2026 at 3:00 PM to Friday, April 30, 2027 at 5:00 PM
Recurs: Runs Nov 22 – Apr 30 (160 days)
Venue: August Wilson African American Cultural Center, 980 Liberty Ave Pittsburgh, PA 15222
Organizer: AWAACC
Description: PEJU ALATISE: I WILL BELONG TO ONLY ME | weekdays 3pm-6pm, weekends 1pm-5pm Exhibition dates are available one month in advance with online sales closing 2 hours before the galleries open each day. Tickets can be purchased on site as a walk-in for same day or future dates. Titled after a line from her own writing, I Will Belong to Only Me marks the first U.S. solo survey of Peju Alatise (b. 1975 in Lagos, Nigeria). A defining figure in contemporary African art, this exhibition brings together two decades of her work across sculpture, installation, text, and film. Anchored by her celebrated installation Flying Girls (2015–16), I Will Belong to Only Me embodies Alatise’s artistic prowess, conceptual depth, and multidisciplinary command across architecture, painting, sculpture, and storytelling. Merging Yorùbá cosmology with poetic form, Alatise builds spaces where imagination is resistance and African girlhood is centered, protected, and celebrated. ABOUT THE ARTIST Peju Alatise (b. 1975, Lagos) is a Nigerian interdisciplinary artist, architect, and author whose practice spans sculpture, installation, painting, film, and fiction. She lives and works between Lagos, Nigeria and Glasgow, UK. Trained in architecture at Ladoke Akintola University of Technology, Alatise began her career balancing architectural work with studio practice. text:

Recurs: Every Wed – Sun, weekly
Venue: Wood Street Galleries, 601 Wood St, Pittsburgh, PA 15222, USA
Organizer: Pittsburgh Cultural Trust
Description: Sound of the City is an immersive audio installation and listening environment by NYC born artist and composer Hprizm, whose practice spans a wide array of genres, including music, performance and multimedia installations. He is a co-founder of the seminal hip-hop group Antipop Consortium, an experimental collective known for their lyrical approach to electronic music.
Centered on a sonic score that moves between abstract noise and melodic interludes, Sound of the City collapses vinyl records, tape loops and granular synthesis with audio footage captured by Hprizm over the past few years. Wielding his phone as a primary recording device, the artist took notice of his sonic environment while traversing New York City and western Pennsylvania, where he partially resides. In his own words, “The sound of the city, in a literal sense, is dense. Buried histories rumble beneath the foundation of brick. Crate digging and knowledge of self unearthed a cultural medium that informs my process.”
For Hprizm, sound carries strong implications—not only about personal narrative, but about socioeconomic conditions and resources as well. He writes, “Within the throughline for most of my work is an interrelation between memory and sonic imprints. Hprizm: Sound of the City takes place on Friday, November 27, 2026 at 11:00 AM at Wood Street Galleries.
Event: Hprizm: Sound of the City
Date: Friday, November 27, 2026 at 11:00 AM to 4:00 PM
Recurs: Every Wed – Sun, weekly
Venue: Wood Street Galleries, 601 Wood St, Pittsburgh, PA 15222, USA
Organizer: Pittsburgh Cultural Trust
Description: Sound of the City is an immersive audio installation and listening environment by NYC born artist and composer Hprizm, whose practice spans a wide array of genres, including music, performance and multimedia installations. He is a co-founder of the seminal hip-hop group Antipop Consortium, an experimental collective known for their lyrical approach to electronic music.
Centered on a sonic score that moves between abstract noise and melodic interludes, Sound of the City collapses vinyl records, tape loops and granular synthesis with audio footage captured by Hprizm over the past few years. Wielding his phone as a primary recording device, the artist took notice of his sonic environment while traversing New York City and western Pennsylvania, where he partially resides. In his own words, “The sound of the city, in a literal sense, is dense. Buried histories rumble beneath the foundation of brick. Crate digging and knowledge of self unearthed a cultural medium that informs my process.”
For Hprizm, sound carries strong implications—not only about personal narrative, but about socioeconomic conditions and resources as well. He writes, “Within the throughline for most of my work is an interrelation between memory and sonic imprints. Over the course of the last few years, with global events in mind, I noticed how much the sonic landscape changed. During the pandemic, the streets were quiet. Description: Time left to complete order Benedum Center The Benedum Center ® , a Pittsburgh Cultural Trust theater, is a focal point of Pittsburgh's Cultural District. The 2,800-seat theater is home to Pittsburgh Cultural Trust presentations including PNC Broadway in Pittsburgh, Dentons Cohen & Grigsby Trust Presents, and First Night Pittsburgh. Organizer: Pittsburgh Cultural Trust
Description: Sound of the City is an immersive audio installation and listening environment by NYC born artist and composer Hprizm, whose practice spans a wide array of genres, including music, performance and multimedia installations. He is a co-founder of the seminal hip-hop group Antipop Consortium, an experimental collective known for their lyrical approach to electronic music.
Centered on a sonic score that moves between abstract noise and melodic interludes, Sound of the City collapses vinyl records, tape loops and granular synthesis with audio footage captured by Hprizm over the past few years. Wielding his phone as a primary recording device, the artist took notice of his sonic environment while traversing New York City and western Pennsylvania, where he partially resides. In his own words, “The sound of the city, in a literal sense, is dense. Buried histories rumble beneath the foundation of brick. Crate digging and knowledge of self unearthed a cultural medium that informs my process.”
For Hprizm, sound carries strong implications—not only about personal narrative, but about socioeconomic conditions and resources as well. He writes, “Within the throughline for most of my work is an interrelation between memory and sonic imprints. Over the course of the last few years, with global events in mind, I noticed how much the sonic landscape changed. During the pandemic, the streets were quiet. Description: Opening night of A Christmas Carol has arrived, the audience is in their seats, and disaster strikes: the entire cast and director are nowhere to be found. Description: The inaugural New Hazlett Theater ForgeWorks production, It’s Just a Smatter of Time, is an interdisciplinary, evening-length work by Ephrat Asherie Dance, author Mo Willems, and Third Coast Percussion. Exploring how time moves forward and backward, plus what we lose or gain along the way, this cross-generational collaboration uses live percussion, visual storytelling, projected imagery, and interactive audience participation to transform internal emotional landscapes into a tangible environment. Incorporating street and club dance forms including breaking, hip hop, house, popping, locking, whacking, and hustle, the artists investigate how we fill our lives while uncovering new modes of expression.

Organizer: Pittsburgh Cultural Trust
Description: Sound of the City is an immersive audio installation and listening environment by NYC born artist and composer Hprizm, whose practice spans a wide array of genres, including music, performance and multimedia installations. He is a co-founder of the seminal hip-hop group Antipop Consortium, an experimental collective known for their lyrical approach to electronic music.
Centered on a sonic score that moves between abstract noise and melodic interludes, Sound of the City collapses vinyl records, tape loops and granular synthesis with audio footage captured by Hprizm over the past few years. Wielding his phone as a primary recording device, the artist took notice of his sonic environment while traversing New York City and western Pennsylvania, where he partially resides. In his own words, “The sound of the city, in a literal sense, is dense. Buried histories rumble beneath the foundation of brick. Crate digging and knowledge of self unearthed a cultural medium that informs my process.”
For Hprizm, sound carries strong implications—not only about personal narrative, but about socioeconomic conditions and resources as well. He writes, “Within the throughline for most of my work is an interrelation between memory and sonic imprints. Recurs: Every Wed – Sun, weekly
Venue: Wood Street Galleries, 601 Wood St, Pittsburgh, PA 15222, USA
Organizer: Pittsburgh Cultural Trust
Description: Sound of the City is an immersive audio installation and listening environment by NYC born artist and composer Hprizm, whose practice spans a wide array of genres, including music, performance and multimedia installations. He is a co-founder of the seminal hip-hop group Antipop Consortium, an experimental collective known for their lyrical approach to electronic music.
Centered on a sonic score that moves between abstract noise and melodic interludes, Sound of the City collapses vinyl records, tape loops and granular synthesis with audio footage captured by Hprizm over the past few years. Wielding his phone as a primary recording device, the artist took notice of his sonic environment while traversing New York City and western Pennsylvania, where he partially resides. In his own words, “The sound of the city, in a literal sense, is dense. Buried histories rumble beneath the foundation of brick. Crate digging and knowledge of self unearthed a cultural medium that informs my process.”
For Hprizm, sound carries strong implications—not only about personal narrative, but about socioeconomic conditions and resources as well. He writes, “Within the throughline for most of my work is an interrelation between memory and sonic imprints. Over the course of the last few years, with global events in mind, I noticed how much the sonic landscape changed. During the pandemic, the streets were quiet. Then there was the sound of unrest and protest. Things went silent again, and then there was

text:

Event: Hprizm: Sound of the City
Date: Saturday, December 12, 2026 at 11:00 AM to 4:00 PM
Recurs: Every Wed – Sun, weekly
Venue: Wood Street Galleries, 601 Wood St, Pittsburgh, PA 15222, USA
Organizer: Pittsburgh Cultural Trust
Description: Sound of the City is an immersive audio installation and listening environment by NYC born artist and composer Hprizm, whose practice spans a wide array of genres, including music, performance and multimedia installations. He is a co-founder of the seminal hip-hop group Antipop Consortium, an experimental collective known for their lyrical approach to electronic music.
Centered on a sonic score that moves between abstract noise and melodic interludes, Sound of the City collapses vinyl records, tape loops and granular synthesis with audio footage captured by Hprizm over the past few years. Wielding his phone as a primary recording device, the artist took notice of his sonic environment while traversing New York City and western Pennsylvania, where he partially resides. In his own words, “The sound of the city, in a literal sense, is dense. Buried histories rumble beneath the foundation of brick. Crate digging and knowledge of self unearthed a cultural medium that informs my process.”
For Hprizm, sound carries strong implications—not only about personal narrative, but about socioeconomic conditions and resources as well. He writes, “Within the throughline for most of my work is an interrelation between memory and sonic imprints. Over the course of the last few years, with global events in mind, I noticed how much the sonic landscape changed. During the pandemic, the streets were quiet. Description: Opening night of A Christmas Carol has arrived, the audience is in their seats, and disaster strikes: the entire cast and director are nowhere to be found. Organizer: Pittsburgh Cultural Trust
Description: Sound of the City is an immersive audio installation and listening environment by NYC born artist and composer Hprizm, whose practice spans a wide array of genres, including music, performance and multimedia installations. He is a co-founder of the seminal hip-hop group Antipop Consortium, an experimental collective known for their lyrical approach to electronic music.
Centered on a sonic score that moves between abstract noise and melodic interludes, Sound of the City collapses vinyl records, tape loops and granular synthesis with audio footage captured by Hprizm over the past few years. Wielding his phone as a primary recording device, the artist took notice of his sonic environment while traversing New York City and western Pennsylvania, where he partially resides. In his own words, “The sound of the city, in a literal sense, is dense. Buried histories rumble beneath the foundation of brick. Crate digging and knowledge of self unearthed a cultural medium that informs my process.”
For Hprizm, sound carries strong implications—not only about personal narrative, but about socioeconomic conditions and resources as well. He writes, “Within the throughline for most of my work is an interrelation between memory and sonic imprints. Over the course of the last few years, with global events in mind, I noticed how much the sonic landscape changed. During the pandemic, the streets were quiet. title: Aaron Lewis (Thursday, December 17, 2026)
text:
Aaron Lewis takes place on Thursday, December 17, 2026 at 7:00 PM at Event Center.
Event: Aaron Lewis
Date: Thursday, December 17, 2026 at 7:00 PM
Venue: Event Center, Cincinnati, OH
Organizer: Hard Rock Casino Cincinnati
Description: Aaron Lewis, the Vermont-born powerhouse first found success with Staind - the 2000s-era hard rockers who injected meditative muscle into an era better known for mindless aggression. But while that band is still very much alive, it was never enough to satisfy Lewis’ creative drive. Embracing his roots to earn a rare second round of success, a series of solo Country projects have led to two No. 1 Billboard Country Album debuts - TOWN LINE (2011) and SINNER (2016) - plus a PLATINUM collab with heroes George Jones and Charlie Daniels (“Country Boy”), and a GOLD-certified Billboard No. 1 with “Am I The Only One” in 2021. Lewis’ 2022 solo album followed suit, with FRAYED AT BOTH ENDS emerging as the best-selling Country album in America but he never wrote songs for the stats. No matter the sonic setting, Lewis writes and sings to get his truth out and his latest album THE HILL (2024) is no different.

title: Hprizm: Sound of the City (Saturday, December 19, 2026)
text:
Hprizm: Sound of the City takes place on Saturday, December 19, 2026 at 11:00 AM at Wood Street Galleries.
Event: Hprizm: Sound of the City
Date: Saturday, December 19, 2026 at 11:00 AM to 4:00 PM
Recurs: Every Wed – Sun, weekly
Venue: Wood Street Galleries, 601 Wood St, Pittsburgh, PA 15222, USA
Organizer: Pittsburgh Cultural Trust
Description: Sound of the City is an immersive audio installation and listening environment by NYC born artist and composer Hprizm, whose practice spans a wide array of genres, including music, performance and multimedia installations. He is a co-founder of the seminal hip-hop group Antipop Consortium, an experimental collective known for their lyrical approach to electronic music.
Centered on a sonic score that moves between abstract noise and melodic interludes, Sound of the City collapses vinyl records, tape loops and granular synthesis with audio footage captured by Hprizm over the past few years. Wielding his phone as a primary recording device, the artist took notice of his sonic environment while traversing New York City and western Pennsylvania, where he partially resides. In his own words, “The sound of the city, in a literal sense, is dense. Buried histories rumble beneath the foundation of brick. Crate digging and knowledge of self unearthed a cultural medium that informs my process.”
For Hprizm, sound carries strong implications—not only about personal narrative, but about socioeconomic conditions and resources as well. He writes, “Within the throughline for most of my work is an interrelation between memory and sonic imprints. title: The Writer's Landscape (Sunday, December 20, 2026)
text:
The Writer's Landscape takes place on Sunday, December 20, 2026 at Harris Theater.
Event: The Writer's Landscape
Date: Sunday, December 20, 2026
Venue: Harris Theater, 980 Liberty Ave Pittsburgh PA 15222
Category: arts
Organizer: August Wilson African American Cultural Center
Description: The August Wilson African American Cultural Center, one of the largest cultural organizations in the country focused exclusively on the African American experience and the arts of the African diaspora, is creating August Wilson: The Writer’s Landscape, the first-ever exhibition dedicated to the life and works of Pulitzer Prize-winning playwright August Wilson. Opening in spring 2022, the 3,600 square foot permanent exhibition will explore the people and places of Pittsburgh, where Wilson was born and raised, and which had a profound impact on shaping his worldview and inspiring his unprecedented 10-play American Century Cycle. Presented in three sections, or acts, August Wilson: The Writer’s Landscape will showcase the universal themes the prolific playwright tackled and the enduring relevance of his work through artifacts from Wilson’s life and notable productions of his work; elements that invite patrons to address the issues of race, representation, family, and community; and interactive digital components that showcase each play in the cycle and where Wilson’s works are being presented around the world today.
Born and raised in Pittsburgh’s Hill District, Wilson drew his greatest inspiration from the city and its people. Many of his works in the American Century Cycle, which almost exclusively take place in Pittsburgh and represent each decade of the 1900s, were largely informed by Wilson’s observations of the environment that surrounded him.

title: A Lyrical Christmas Carol (Sunday, December 20, 2026)
text:
A Lyrical Christmas Carol runs from Sunday, December 20, 2026 to Thursday, December 24, 2026 at Pittsburgh Cultural Trust.
Event: A Lyrical Christmas Carol
Date: Sunday, December 20, 2026 at 7:30 PM to Thursday, December 24, 2026
Recurs: Runs Dec 20 – Dec 24 (5 days)
Venue: Pittsburgh Cultural Trust, 327 S Main St, Pittsburgh, PA 15220
Category: Family
Organizer: Pittsburgh Musical Theater
Description: Young Artist Production

Adapted for the Stage by: Ken & Jane Gargaro
Based on the book by Charles Dickens

A holiday tradition since 1990!

On Christmas Eve, Scrooge sits in his house with not a kind word for anyone; he just wants to be left alone until the "humbug" of Christmas is over. But four ghostly visitors - his former business partner, followed by the Ghosts of Christmas Past, Christmas Present, and Christmas Yet to Come - show him the error of his ways, and by the time Christmas Day dawns, Scrooge is a changed person. The entire family will enjoy this timeless classic and Pittsburgh tradition, featuring your favorite holiday carols!

What is a Young Artist Production?
The foundation of PMT’s mission is built on arts education, development, mentorship, and providing performance opportunities for young artists. Students at PMT Conservatory receive a truly unique experience to use their training in fully produced productions of their own in which they take on roles as performers and technical theater crew. Whether a student wishes to pursue a career in the arts or another field, Young Artist Productions provide an opportunity for growth and building transferable life skills in our future leaders. Patrons attending Young Artist Productions will be a part of it all as they experience and enjoy the best of our region’s talented youth in professional-quality entertainment!

title: Hprizm: Sound of the City (Wednesday, December 23, 2026)
text:

Date: Wednesday, December 23, 2026 at 11:00 AM to 4:00 PM
Recurs: Every Wed – Sun, weekly
Venue: Wood Street Galleries, 601 Wood St, Pittsburgh, PA 15222, USA
Organizer: Pittsburgh Cultural Trust
Description: Sound of the City is an immersive audio installation and listening environment by NYC born artist and composer Hprizm, whose practice spans a wide array of genres, including music, performance and multimedia installations. He is a co-founder of the seminal hip-hop group Antipop Consortium, an experimental collective known for their lyrical approach to electronic music.
Centered on a sonic score that moves between abstract noise and melodic interludes, Sound of the City collapses vinyl records, tape loops and granular synthesis with audio footage captured by Hprizm over the past few years. Wielding his phone as a primary recording device, the artist took notice of his sonic environment while traversing New York City and western Pennsylvania, where he partially resides. In his own words, “The sound of the city, in a literal sense, is dense. Buried histories rumble beneath the foundation of brick. Crate digging and knowledge of self unearthed a cultural medium that informs my process.”
For Hprizm, sound carries strong implications—not only about personal narrative, but about socioeconomic conditions and resources as well. He writes, “Within the throughline for most of my work is an interrelation between memory and sonic imprints. Over the course of the last few years, with global events in mind, I noticed how much the sonic landscape changed. During the pandemic, the streets were quiet. Organizer: Pittsburgh Cultural Trust
Description: Sound of the City is an immersive audio installation and listening environment by NYC born artist and composer Hprizm, whose practice spans a wide array of genres, including music, performance and multimedia installations. He is a co-founder of the seminal hip-hop group Antipop Consortium, an experimental collective known for their lyrical approach to electronic music.
Centered on a sonic score that moves between abstract noise and melodic interludes, Sound of the City collapses vinyl records, tape loops and granular synthesis with audio footage captured by Hprizm over the past few years. Wielding his phone as a primary recording device, the artist took notice of his sonic environment while traversing New York City and western Pennsylvania, where he partially resides. In his own words, “The sound of the city, in a literal sense, is dense. Buried histories rumble beneath the foundation of brick. Crate digging and knowledge of self unearthed a cultural medium that informs my process.”
For Hprizm, sound carries strong implications—not only about personal narrative, but about socioeconomic conditions and resources as well. He writes, “Within the throughline for most of my work is an interrelation between memory and sonic imprints. title: August Wilson: The Writer’s Landscape - AWAACC (Friday, January 1, 2027)
text:
August Wilson: The Writer’s Landscape - AWAACC takes place on Friday, January 1, 2027 at August Wilson African American Cultural Center.
Event: August Wilson: The Writer’s Landscape - AWAACC
Date: Friday, January 1, 2027 to 11:59 PM
Venue: August Wilson African American Cultural Center, 980 Liberty Ave, Pittsburgh, PA 15222, USA
Organizer: August Wilson African American Cultural Center
Description: "August Wilson: The Writer’s Landscape" is the first-ever permanent exhibition dedicated to Pulitzer Prize-winning playwright August Wilson, exploring how his Pittsburgh upbringing profoundly shaped his acclaimed American Century Cycle. This 3,600-square-foot exhibit guides visitors through three acts: "The Coffee Shop," inspired by his early observational writing, a replica of "The Office" showcasing his personal items and manuscripts, and "The Street," a recreation of Pittsburgh’s Hill District featuring an interactive map, video, and authentic props and costumes from his Broadway productions. Attendees will gain insight into major themes from his plays and discover the timeless relevance of his artistic legacy.

Description: Sound of the City is an immersive audio installation and listening environment by NYC born artist and composer Hprizm, whose practice spans a wide array of genres, including music, performance and multimedia installations. He is a co-founder of the seminal hip-hop group Antipop Consortium, an experimental collective known for their lyrical approach to electronic music.
Centered on a sonic score that moves between abstract noise and melodic interludes, Sound of the City collapses vinyl records, tape loops and granular synthesis with audio footage captured by Hprizm over the past few years. Wielding his phone as a primary recording device, the artist took notice of his sonic environment while traversing New York City and western Pennsylvania, where he partially resides. In his own words, “The sound of the city, in a literal sense, is dense. Buried histories rumble beneath the foundation of brick. Crate digging and knowledge of self unearthed a cultural medium that informs my process.”
For Hprizm, sound carries strong implications—not only about personal narrative, but about socioeconomic conditions and resources as well. He writes, “Within the throughline for most of my work is an interrelation between memory and sonic imprints. In his own words, “The sound of the city, in a literal sense, is dense. Buried histories rumble beneath the foundation of brick. text:

Recurs: Every Wed – Sun, weekly
Venue: Wood Street Galleries, 601 Wood St, Pittsburgh, PA 15222, USA
Organizer: Pittsburgh Cultural Trust
Description: Sound of the City is an immersive audio installation and listening environment by NYC born artist and composer Hprizm, whose practice spans a wide array of genres, including music, performance and multimedia installations. He is a co-founder of the seminal hip-hop group Antipop Consortium, an experimental collective known for their lyrical approach to electronic music.
Centered on a sonic score that moves between abstract noise and melodic interludes, Sound of the City collapses vinyl records, tape loops and granular synthesis with audio footage captured by Hprizm over the past few years. Wielding his phone as a primary recording device, the artist took notice of his sonic environment while traversing New York City and western Pennsylvania, where he partially resides. In his own words, “The sound of the city, in a literal sense, is dense. Buried histories rumble beneath the foundation of brick. Crate digging and knowledge of self unearthed a cultural medium that informs my process.”
For Hprizm, sound carries strong implications—not only about personal narrative, but about socioeconomic conditions and resources as well. He writes, “Within the throughline for most of my work is an interrelation between memory and sonic imprints. title: Hprizm: Sound of the City (Wednesday, January 20, 2027)
text:
Hprizm: Sound of the City takes place on Wednesday, January 20, 2027 at 11:00 AM at Wood Street Galleries.
Event: Hprizm: Sound of the City
Date: Wednesday, January 20, 2027 at 11:00 AM to 4:00 PM
Recurs: Every Wed – Sun, weekly
Venue: Wood Street Galleries, 601 Wood St, Pittsburgh, PA 15222, USA
Organizer: Pittsburgh Cultural Trust
Description: Sound of the City is an immersive audio installation and listening environment by NYC born artist and composer Hprizm, whose practice spans a wide array of genres, including music, performance and multimedia installations. He is a co-founder of the seminal hip-hop group Antipop Consortium, an experimental collective known for their lyrical approach to electronic music.
Centered on a sonic score that moves between abstract noise and melodic interludes, Sound of the City collapses vinyl records, tape loops and granular synthesis with audio footage captured by Hprizm over the past few years. Wielding his phone as a primary recording device, the artist took notice of his sonic environment while traversing New York City and western Pennsylvania, where he partially resides. In his own words, “The sound of the city, in a literal sense, is dense. Buried histories rumble beneath the foundation of brick. Crate digging and knowledge of self unearthed a cultural medium that informs my process.”
For Hprizm, sound carries strong implications—not only about personal narrative, but about socioeconomic conditions and resources as well. He writes, “Within the throughline for most of my work is an interrelation between memory and sonic imprints. Over the course of the last few years, with global events in mind, I noticed how much the sonic landscape changed. During the pandemic, the streets were quiet. Venue: Heinz Hall for the Performing Arts, 600 Penn Avenue, Pittsburgh, PA 15222
Category: arts, music
Organizer: Pittsburgh Symphony Orchestra
Price: 130
Description: Dolly Parton's music comes to Pittsburgh in Dolly Parton's Threads: My Songs In Symphony, an innovative multimedia experience featuring Dolly on screen and taking audiences in a visual-musical journey of her songs, her life, and her stories. With a cast of phenomenal guest vocalists and musicians, the Pittsburgh Symphony Orchestra performs new and innovative orchestrations by David Hamilton, including hits such as "Jolene," "Coat Of Many Colors," and "I Will Always Love You," in addition to Dolly's personal favorites and a selection from her upcoming Broadway musical.
Co-produced by Dolly Parton together with Schirmer Theatrical and Sony Music Publishing.
Pittsburgh Symphony Orchestra has partnered with the Dollywood Foundation so that $1 per ticket goes to support Dolly Parton's Imagination Library. Learn more at Imaginationlibrary.com.

title: Hprizm: Sound of the City (Wednesday, January 27, 2027)
text:

Event: Hprizm: Sound of the City
Date: Wednesday, January 27, 2027 at 11:00 AM to 4:00 PM
Recurs: Every Wed – Sun, weekly
Venue: Wood Street Galleries, 601 Wood St, Pittsburgh, PA 15222, USA
Organizer: Pittsburgh Cultural Trust
Description: Sound of the City is an immersive audio installation and listening environment by NYC born artist and composer Hprizm, whose practice spans a wide array of genres, including music, performance and multimedia installations. He is a co-founder of the seminal hip-hop group Antipop Consortium, an experimental collective known for their lyrical approach to electronic music.
Centered on a sonic score that moves between abstract noise and melodic interludes, Sound of the City collapses vinyl records, tape loops and granular synthesis with audio footage captured by Hprizm over the past few years. Wielding his phone as a primary recording device, the artist took notice of his sonic environment while traversing New York City and western Pennsylvania, where he partially resides. In his own words, “The sound of the city, in a literal sense, is dense. Buried histories rumble beneath the foundation of brick. Crate digging and knowledge of self unearthed a cultural medium that informs my process.”
For Hprizm, sound carries strong implications—not only about personal narrative, but about socioeconomic conditions and resources as well. He writes, “Within the throughline for most of my work is an interrelation between memory and sonic imprints. Over the course of the last few years, with global events in mind, I noticed how much the sonic landscape changed. During the pandemic, the streets were quiet. text:

Event: Hprizm: Sound of the City
Date: Sunday, January 31, 2027 at 11:00 AM to 4:00 PM
Recurs: Every Wed – Sun, weekly
Venue: Wood Street Galleries, 601 Wood St, Pittsburgh, PA 15222, USA
Organizer: Pittsburgh Cultural Trust
Description: Sound of the City is an immersive audio installation and listening environment by NYC born artist and composer Hprizm, whose practice spans a wide array of genres, including music, performance and multimedia installations. He is a co-founder of the seminal hip-hop group Antipop Consortium, an experimental collective known for their lyrical approach to electronic music.
Centered on a sonic score that moves between abstract noise and melodic interludes, Sound of the City collapses vinyl records, tape loops and granular synthesis with audio footage captured by Hprizm over the past few years. Wielding his phone as a primary recording device, the artist took notice of his sonic environment while traversing New York City and western Pennsylvania, where he partially resides. In his own words, “The sound of the city, in a literal sense, is dense. Buried histories rumble beneath the foundation of brick. Crate digging and knowledge of self unearthed a cultural medium that informs my process.”
For Hprizm, sound carries strong implications—not only about personal narrative, but about socioeconomic conditions and resources as well. He writes, “Within the throughline for most of my work is an interrelation between memory and sonic imprints. Over the course of the last few years, with global events in mind, I noticed how much the sonic landscape changed. During the pandemic, the streets were quiet. title: Bianca Del Rio: It Gets Bitter - World Comedy Tour (Saturday, February 27, 2027)
text:

Date: Saturday, February 27, 2027 at 8:00 PM
Venue: Seating Chart, 101 6th Street Pittsburgh PA 15222
Organizer: Trust and Outback Presents
Description: TICKET LIMIT : 8 per customer Get ready to swallow a jagged pill of truth because the "Clown in a Gown" is back and meaner than ever. Bianca Del Rio returns to the global stage with her seventh solo stand-up tour, "It Gets Bitter". This milestone trek isn't just another night of comedy; it’s a celebration of 30 years of professional drag excellence and three decades of Bianca absolutely hating everything you stand for. Expect a masterclass in vitriol as the RuPaul’s Drag Race winner turns her razor-sharp tongue toward the absolute absurdity of modern life. From the vapid landscape of pop culture to the chaotic state of world events, and—most importantly—the mundane things people do every day that drive her to the brink, no topic is off-limits and no ego is too big to be deflated. A Stern Warning: If you are sensitive, easily offended, or possess a fragile sense of self-worth, do not select seats near the stage. In classic Bianca fashion, the front row is a firing squad, and no one is safe from her legendary biting insults and lightning-fast wit. She’s seasoned, she’s legendary, and she’s officially exhausted by your nonsense. The old saying is "It gets better", but Bianca is proof that after 30 years in tights "It Gets Bitter"!! The views and opinions expressed in the performance do not necessarily reflect those of the Pittsburgh Cultural Trust. The Trust is committed to its core values of diversity, equity, inclusion, and accessibility, including freedom of expression. Price

Description: Over the past decade, Sanjeev has headlined Las Vegas stages, performed on national TV, and spoken at the world’s biggest companies. As a cognitive scientist from Berkeley, his research explores how magicians use language to influence choices, and even rewrite memories.

title: Girls (Friday, March 5, 2027)
text:
Girls takes place on Friday, March 5, 2027 at 10:00 AM at New Hazlett Theater.
Event: Girls
Date: Friday, March 5, 2027 at 10:00 AM to 7:30 PM
Recurs: On 2 selected dates
Venue: New Hazlett Theater, 6 Allegheny Square E, Pittsburgh, PA 15212, USA
Organizer: New Hazlett Theater
Price: 37
Description: GIRLS by Maya Anabella is an unfiltered series of confessions that pulls back the curtain on girlhood. Told from the perspectives of five young women, the production relies on the pure power of words to tackle life's heaviest, most authentic topics. By saying the quiet parts out loud, the piece navigates the raw realities of the modern female experience. Fusing sharp wit with vulnerable truths, the performance offers an uncompromising look into girlhood, confronting body image, societal double standards, and the silent struggles of youth. What begins as isolated stories transforms into a fierce declaration of strength. Up close and personal, the piece is a moving reminder that our flaws shape exactly who we are, and no matter what, we are never alone. Girlhood isn't something you can understand unless you experience it. It's time to experience GIRLS.

Description: The Iconic Love Story Live on Stage

A breathtaking musical epic featuring an unforgettable score including “The Heat Is On in Saigon,” “The Movie in My Mind,” “Last Night of the World,” and “I’d Give My Life for You.” This powerful story of love, sacrifice, and survival has captivated audiences around the world for generations.

In the chaotic final days of the Vietnam War, a doomed romance changes two lives forever. Kim, a resilient young Vietnamese orphan, meets Chris, a disillusioned American Marine, at a bustling Saigon nightclub. Torn apart by the sudden, historic Fall of Saigon, they embark on an epic, multi-year journey of survival. Powered by a legendary, sung-through score, Miss Saigon is a staggering portrait of a mother's fierce devotion and the enduring strength of the human spirit amidst broken places.

Music by Claude-Michel Schönberg
Lyrics by Alain Boublil, Richard Maltby, Jr.

Miss Saigon is licensed by Music Theatre International (MTI) www.mtishows.com by arrangement with CAMERON MACKINTOSH LTD.

title: Phantom of the Opera (Sunday, March 28, 2027)
text:
Phantom of the Opera runs from Sunday, March 28, 2027 to Thursday, April 8, 2027 at Seating Chart.
Event: Phantom of the Opera
Date: Sunday, March 28, 2027 at 7:30 PM to Thursday, April 8, 2027
Recurs: Runs Mar 28 – Apr 8 (12 days)
Venue: Seating Chart, 7th Street and Penn Ave Pittsburgh PA 15222
Organizer: PNC Broadway in Pittsburgh
Description: The brilliant original returns “more spectacular than event” - Sunday Express The Phantom is back to thrill audiences once again! Cameron Mackintosh presents a revitalized new production of Andrew Lloyd Webber’s legendary musical, PHANTOM OF THE OPERA, which was rapturously received by London critics when it reopened in 2021. Featuring Maria Björnson’s brilliant original design and based on the celebrated direction of Harold Prince, with musical staging and choreography by Gillian Lynne, the new PHANTOM North American tour comes to the Benedum Center. PHANTOM OF THE OPERA is widely considered one of the most beautiful and spectacular productions in history, playing to over 160 million people in 47 territories and 195 cities in 21 languages. Andrew Lloyd Webber’s romantic, haunting, and soaring score includes “The Music of the Night,” “All I Ask of You,” “Wishing You Were Somehow Here Again,” “Masquerade,” and the iconic title song. It tells the tale of a disfigured musical genius known only as ‘The Phantom’ who haunts the depths of the Paris Opera House. Mesmerized by the talents and beauty of a young soprano, Christine, The Phantom lures her as his protégé and falls fiercely in love with her. Unaware of Christine’s love for Raoul, The Phantom’s obsession sets the scene for a dramatic turn of events where jealousy, madness, and passions collide. Produced by CAMERON MACKINTOSH with LW ENTERTAINMENT.

title: The Women Who Lit the Way (Friday, April 16, 2027)
text:
The Women Who Lit the Way takes place on Friday, April 16, 2027 at 10:00 AM at New Hazlett Theater.
Event: The Women Who Lit the Way
Date: Friday, April 16, 2027 at 10:00 AM to 7:30 PM
Recurs: On 2 selected dates
Venue: New Hazlett Theater, 6 Allegheny Square E, Pittsburgh, PA 15212, USA
Organizer: Bootstrap Design Co.
Price: 37
Description: The Women Who Lit the Way by Omari Abdul-Alim is an immersive interdisciplinary fusion celebrating the legacy of Pittsburgh legends O'Labrice Beckom and Henrietta Freeman. Composed by Omarimhotep, directed by Dominique Briggs, and choreographed by Kontara Morphis, the production brings six Beckom Freeman residency alumni together with selected student performers from the Guardians of Sound Hip Hop Orchestra. Under Omari Abdul-Alim’s artistic direction, the program weaves violin, voice, spoken word, emceeing, dance, and rhythm section performance into an electric journey through history. More than a standard tribute, it brings together generations of artists to spotlight local talent and celebrate the Black teaching artists who shape Pittsburgh's cultural landscape.

title: 3rd International Conference on Stem Cells, Regenerative Medicine & Tissue Engineering (Monday, April 19, 2027)
text:
3rd International Conference on Stem Cells, Regenerative Medicine & Tissue Engineering runs from Monday, April 19, 2027 to Tuesday, April 20, 2027 at Milton Hall.
Event: 3rd International Conference on Stem Cells, Regenerative Medicine & Tissue Engineering
Date: Monday, April 19, 2027 at 9:30 AM to Tuesday, April 20, 2027 at 6:30 PM
Recurs: Runs Apr 19 – Apr 20 (2 days)
Venue: Milton Hall, Ridge Ave, Pittsburgh, PA 15212, USA
Organizer: PAGES
Description: Following the success of our previous conferences, we are delighted to announce the 3rd International Conference on Stem Cells, Regenerative Medicine & Tissue Engineering (STEMCELL-2027), which will take place on April 19–20, 2027 in Milan, Italy. STEMCELL-2027 aims to bring together leading scientists, researchers, clinicians, academicians, and industry professionals from around the world to share knowledge, discuss emerging research, and promote global collaborations in the rapidly advancing fields of stem cell science and regenerative medicine. The conference will highlight the latest developments in stem cell biology, regenerative therapies, tissue engineering, cellular technologies, and clinical applications. Participants will gain valuable insights into innovative research, technological advancements, and future directions shaping modern biomedical science. The scientific program will feature keynote lectures, plenary sessions, oral and poster presentations, and networking opportunities, providing an excellent platform for participants to exchange ideas, present their research, and build international partnerships. We warmly invite researchers, healthcare professionals, industry experts, and students to join us in Milan, Italy, for STEMCELL-2027 and contribute to advancing the future of regenerative medicine and global healthcare.
Best Regards, R Gayathri | Conference Secretary

Venue: Byham Theater, 101 6th St, Pittsburgh, PA 15222, USA

Description: The Pittsburgh Cultural Trust presents a vibrant calendar of ballet and dance performances, alongside diverse visual arts exhibitions. Attendees can experience a wide range of dance, from cultural experiences like TAARi The African Experience and contemporary works by A.I.M. by Kyle Abraham, to classical ballets such as *A Midsummer Night's Dream* and *The Nutcracker* (including a sensory-friendly option), alongside celebrity shows like Derek Hough's *Symphony of Dance*. Complementing the stage, galleries showcase compelling exhibitions on topics ranging from Frank Lloyd Wright's regional impact and Michael Zagaris's NFL photography to contemporary art by Sharmistha Ray and a Juried Visual Arts Exhibition. This curated schedule offers enriching cultural experiences for diverse audiences across various venues.

title: Shikeith, Hold (Thursday, April 29, 2027)
text:
Shikeith, Hold runs from Thursday, April 29, 2027 to Wednesday, June 30, 2027 at Arts Landing.
Event: Shikeith, Hold
Date: Thursday, April 29, 2027 to Wednesday, June 30, 2027
Recurs: Runs Apr 29 – Jun 30 (63 days)
Venue: Arts Landing, 805 Liberty Ave, Pittsburgh, PA 15222, USA
Organizer: Pittsburgh Cultural Trust
Price: 0
Description: Installed at Arts Landing, Hold is made of weathering steel and neon. The sculpture extends Project Blue Space, Shikeith’s initiative exploring the spiritual, cultural, and political relationships Black communities have forged with water. Its title gestures toward both the hold of a slave ship and the body as a vessel of memory, feeling, and endurance. Within, the work glows haint blue, a color rooted in Gullah Geechee traditions of protection. Its light pulses like breath. Over time, the steel exterior will deepen and shift with weather. About the Artist Shikeith is a visual artist and filmmaker whose work explores psychological landscapes and how history persists in the present. Hold, his first public art commission, brings this inquiry into civic space. Hold by Shikeith is commissioned by the Pittsburgh Cultural Trust for Arts Landing. Hold is developed as part of Project Blue Space, a web-based platform mapping the cultural, spiritual, and political relationships Black communities have forged with water. The project is funded by the Mellon Foundation’s Humanities in Place initiative.

title: Distant Worlds: Music from FINAL FANTASY – Eternal (Saturday, July 31, 2027)
text:
Distant Worlds: Music from FINAL FANTASY – Eternal takes place on Saturday, July 31, 2027 at 7:30 PM at Heinz Hall for the Performing Arts.
Event: Distant Worlds: Music from FINAL FANTASY – Eternal
Date: Saturday, July 31, 2027 at 7:30 PM
Venue: Heinz Hall for the Performing Arts, 600 Penn Avenue Pittsburgh PA 15222
Category: arts
Organizer: Pittsburgh Symphony Orchestra
Description: FINAL FANTASY 40th Anniversary Distant Worlds: music from FINAL FANTASY – Eternal

Were you there forty years ago when the “Prelude” played for the first time? Were you there thirty years ago when “Opening - Bombing Mission” first brought players to Midgar? Whether your adventures started in Cornelia, Eorzea, Valisthea, or elsewhere, we invite you and your fellow warriors of light to continue your journey with this new concert series.

Our special 40th anniversary program celebrates the enduring music of Nobuo Uematsu, Masashi Hamauzu, Naoshi Mizuta, Hitoshi Sakimoto, Yoko Shimomura, and Masayoshi Soken, brought to life by a full orchestra and chorus and conducted by Maestro Arnie Roth. HD videos created by SQUARE ENIX accompany the music, celebrating four decades of FINAL FANTASY and the evolution of video game technology.
